caption:
is washing your face with hot water bad?

Hot water doesn't wash your face any better.

Hot, lukewarm or cold: what do you use? One word below.

In a small study, the same cleanser was put on the skin at 4°C, 20°C and 40°C once a day for four days. The warmer it was, the more irritated the skin got: more redness, and more water escaping through the skin barrier.

It used a strong test cleanser on forearms, in 10 people, so treat it as a hint, not a verdict. But it fits what many people notice: a very hot wash can leave the face red and tight.

Try two weeks of lukewarm water for your face and see if the tight feeling eases.

Send this to the one whose showers could boil an egg.

General education only. If your skin stays red, burning or flaky, see a doctor in person.
